target_domain: Origin-of-life biochemistry and prebiotic chemistry concerned with why biological systems require homochirality, including chiral symmetry breaking, molecular recognition, peptide/protein assembly function, and electron transfer.
core_gap: Existing work explains chiral amplification in specialized reactions, network-level symmetry breaking, and partial prebiotic stability of homochiral peptides, but it does not provide a general quantitative mechanism linking homochirality to life-required functions such as electron transfer, molecular recognition, catalytic specificity, replication fidelity, and cross-polymer coordination, nor does it establish whether chirality is universally necessary or contingent under alternative definitions of life.
